heading: Congressional findings and declaration of purpose

tree.heading: Abusive practices
tree.text: There is abundant evidence of the use of abusive, deceptive, and unfair debt collection practices by many debt collectors. Abusive debt collection practices contribute to the number of personal bankruptcies, to marital instability, to the loss of jobs, and to invasions of individual privacy.

tree.heading: Inadequacy of laws
tree.text: Existing laws and procedures for redressing these injuries are inadequate to protect consumers.

tree.heading: Available non-abusive collection methods
tree.text: Means other than misrepresentation or other abusive debt collection practices are available for the effective collection of debts.

tree.heading: Interstate commerce
tree.text: Abusive debt collection practices are carried on to a substantial extent in interstate commerce and through means and instrumentalities of such commerce. Even where abusive debt collection practices are purely intrastate in character, they nevertheless directly affect interstate commerce.

tree.heading: Purposes
tree.text: It is the purpose of this subchapter to eliminate abusive debt collection practices by debt collectors, to insure that those debt collectors who refrain from using abusive debt collection practices are not competitively disadvantaged, and to promote consistent State action to protect consumers against debt collection abuses.

notes.text: Effective DatePub. L. 90–321, title VIII, § 819, formerly § 818, as added by Pub. L. 95–109, Sept. 20, 1977, 91 Stat. 883, § 818; renumbered § 819, Pub. Short TitleThis subchapter known as the “Fair Debt Collection Practices Act”, see Short Title note set out under section 1601 of this title.
